input.quote: 13.1 IBM assumes and will assume ownership and MSL assigns and will assign all intellectual and industrial property rights for hardware, software, design and documentation of all Products delivered under this Agreement
input.rationale:
The IP bargain runs in our favour and meets the preferred position on its material terms. Section 13.1 (p0197) gives IBM ownership of, and MSL a present and future assignment of, all intellectual and industrial property rights in the hardware, software, design and documentation of all Products delivered, and p0198 extends IBM ownership/MSL assignment to MSL inventions on Products and on IBM processes and systems, with MSL's retained use limited to performing its obligations here. Ownership is stronger than the fallback licence, so the fallback licence elements (perpetual/irrevocable/worldwide/royalty-free use, modify, sublicense) are subsumed. MSL keeps generic production tooling (p1088: "Tools commonly used in production and/or Integration will be owned and managed by MSL"), which the playbook expressly permits. Any MSL licence in IBM information is confined to service delivery: 13.3(a) (p0208) grants MSL only "a royalty-free license to use the confidential information disclosed in connection with this Agreement ... necessary to manufacture Products solely for IBM", and any other licence to IBM IP requires a separate signed agreement; IBM material and confidential media must be returned on termination (p0130). There is no joint ownership anywhere, and no assignment of IBM IP or data to MSL, so no walk-away trigger. Minor points noted only, not redlined: the Agreement contains no express "MSL retains its pre-existing IP" sentence (a Vendor-side omission that does not prejudice us), no standalone Customer Data ownership sentence, and 24.1(a) (p1136) states MSL conveys no licence under its own IP in the I/T systems context — a residual-risk point that is overridden for delivered Products by the 13.1 assignment. The AECI residuals clause (p1482) is a confidentiality-side mechanic and is addressed under the confidentiality rule, not IP.</rationale>
